This is the dish every British fridge-full-of-leftovers eventually becomes, and the one that explains why the recipe exists at all: the cake is the plate, the egg is the sauce, and together they are a complete breakfast from nothing. skeleton:
Bubble and Squeak with Fried Eggs

British · Easy · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The bubble-and-squeak master's most famous pairing, given its own record because the pairing changes the cooking: when a fried egg lands on top, the bubble cake's job shifts from side dish to foundation — it must be shaped thicker, crusted harder, and fried in more fat, because it is about to be sauced by a yolk and eaten as the plate's centre rather than its edge. This is the dish every British fridge-full-of-leftovers eventually becomes, and the one that explains why the recipe exists at all: the cake is the plate, the egg is the sauce, and together they are a complete breakfast from nothing. The technique builds directly on the master — same cold-dry mix, same slow crust — with two additions: individual cake shaping (one substantial cake per person, 3 cm thick) and the double-fry finish, where the egg cooks in the same pan's fat and the yolk is broken at the table and worked into the crust's fissures.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The bubble cakes

The eggs

To serve

- **The master's two laws hold unchanged:** cold, dry potato and squeezed-dry cabbage. Warm mash glues; wet cabbage steams. If the leftovers are coming straight from a roast dinner, chill everything at least an hour first — the dish is planned leftovers, not improvised ones. - **Shape two substantial cakes, not eight small ones** — about 300 g each, 8–9 cm across, 3 cm thick, pressed firm. The cake must carry an egg and survive a fork worked through it; a thin cake shatters under the payload. - **The 20-minute chill** before frying, as ever. The egg stage's pan and butter sit ready while the second crust builds.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Cakes: 3 cm thick, chilled firm, dual crusts at medium-low, centre steaming hot throughout, at 75 °C for 30 seconds.
  • Eggs: basted in the pan's accumulated fat, whites set, yolks running.
  • Assembly: eggs draped, yolk broken at the table, worked into the crust.

Bubble and Squeak with Fried Eggs

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 25 minutes · Total: 35 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The bubble cakes

  • 500 g cold cooked floury potatoes, roughly mashed
  • 250 g cold cooked cabbage or sprouts, squeezed very dry
  • 30 g butter, softened, plus 30 g for frying
  • 2 spring onions, sliced (30 g)
  • 40 g mature Cheddar, grated (optional)
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 0.5 g grated nutmeg

The eggs

  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 15 ml / 14 g neutral oil (to buffer the butter at egg heat)

To serve

  • Brown breakfast sauce
  • 2 slices (140 g) thick toast, or fried bread's last stand
  • A grilled tomato half each (optional)

Instructions

  1. **Mix, shape, chill.** Combine the potato, cabbage, spring onion, butter, cheese, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until the mix holds when squeezed. Shape two 3 cm-thick cakes, pressing firmly. Chill 20 minutes. Checkpoint — each cake holds a clean edge and feels compact and firm; a thumb pressed in the centre leaves a slow-filling dent, not a crumble.
  2. **First crust — 8 minutes, undisturbed.** Heat the frying butter in a heavy pan over medium-low until foaming. Lay in the cakes and leave them entirely alone 7–8 minutes, until the undersides build a deep, continuous crust. Checkpoint — the edges show deep gold creeping up the sides, and a fish slide passes fully under each cake with crisp resistance — the feeling of a bonded crust, not a sticky base.
  3. **Flip and second crust — 6–7 minutes.** Flip each cake with a confident single turn (they are sturdier than the master's whole-pan version — one spatula does it). Add a small knob of butter (10 g) around the edges for the second face. Cook 6–7 minutes to a matching crust. Checkpoint — both faces deep golden, the sides showing no raw ring, and a cake is steaming hot throughout, with its centre held at 75 °C for 30 seconds on a clean probe — hot through, which matters more with a thick cake than a thin one.
  4. **The eggs in the same pan, 3 minutes.** Lift the cakes to warm plates. Add the oil and the last of the butter to the pan's residual fat and fry the 4 eggs over medium heat to the butter-basted master's spec — basting the hot fat over the whites until set, 2–3 minutes, yolks liquid. Checkpoint — set whites, lace edges, running yolks — and the eggs carry the pan's whole history: butter, crust fond, the faint sweetness of the cabbage's edges. The pan has seasoned its own sauce.
  5. **Landing — two eggs per cake, yolk broken at the table.** Two fried eggs draped across each hot cake, pepper over, sauce and toast alongside. The first cut breaks the yolks, and the eater works the yolk down into the crust's cracks with the fork's edge — the dish's ritual and its whole point. Checkpoint — the eating test: the crust crackles under the fork, the yolk disappears into its fissures, and every forkful from the first to the last carries egg, crust, and the soft cabbage-sweet middle. The plate is complete, and it was leftovers twelve hours ago.

Finish & Plate

Brown sauce at the side (its fruit-sharpness against the yolk's richness), toast to catch what escapes, and tea. This is the Monday plate that closes the Sunday roast's circle — the same cabbage, the same mash, transformed by a crust and an egg into a dish nobody calls leftovers.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cake collapsed to hash under the eggsToo thin or under-chilled3 cm, pressed firm, the full 20-minute chill
Crust tore at the flipTurned early or wet mixThe full 8 minutes; squeeze the cabbage harder
Yolk cooked before the cake's second sideSequencing invertedCakes finish first and hold warm; eggs always last
Centre coldThick cake rushedMedium-low; check the centre is steaming hot throughout and hold at 75 °C for 30 seconds

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Refrigerate the mix and use within 2 days of originally cooking the ingredients** and shaped cakes freeze 2 months (cook from frozen, +4 minutes a side at lower heat). Cook until steaming hot throughout and serve straight away; leftovers used in the mix should be reheated only once. - **Variation — the Benedict bridge:** one poached egg and a spoon of the blender hollandaise replaces the fried eggs — the bubble-and-squeak eggs benedict's whole idea in a sentence. - **Variation — the ham pocket:** press 50 g of chopped leftover ham into each cake's centre at shaping — the roast dinner's full inventory, enclosed. - **The loop:** this record, the master, the cakes, and the benedict are one dish in four forms — the fridge's context decides which one you are cooking.
